In Hotels With Great Taste, we’re pulling back the curtain for a peek at the “special sauce” that hotels use to create memorable, meaningful culinary experiences for their guests.

Look closely at the lodgings that make up Dawn Ranch and you’ll notice they’re actually a patchwork of historic structures in different shapes and sizes. Each building at the luxe 15-acre Russian River resort, which is nestled amongst the towering redwoods in the petite town of Guerneville, California, is linked to a different era of the property’s past.

Built in 1905, it was originally Murphy’s Ranch, a getaway for well-to-do families that operated for seven decades. Later it served for more than 20 years as the pioneering gay resort Fife’s. Today, it’s a refined wine country escape that exists at the crossroads of nature and high-end luxury. The hotel is situated in a floodway, which limits construction for safety purposes, so since 1993 the site’s various owners haven’t been able to build anew; renovating ad infinitum has proven to be just dandy though.

In fact, this limitation turns out to be central to Dawn Ranch’s retro, summer camp-adjacent charm, which feels like a happy throwback even with its modernized facilities and amenities. Spectacularly refurbished in 2023, the current upscale iteration features 81 California-cool rooms, a tremendous spa, a fine-dining restaurant that may very well become impossible to book once word gets out, and a thoughtful, dynamic wine program that highlights some of the world’s most unique bottles.

Rachel Tepper Paley

Rachel Tepper Paley

The property and rooms

When it comes to bunking, you have choices that span a hodgepodge of rustic-chic cabins, chalets, cottages, bungalows, and glamping tents. On the main campus, cabins are cozy and compact, while the cottages and chalets offer more space. Most include private outdoor decks, equally ideal for taking in a morning cuppa or an evening tipple. The bungalows are the roomiest accommodation, outfitted for families and large groups with two bedrooms, two baths, a full kitchen, and gas fireplaces. Across the street, the resort’s Grove campus offers more options, which range from snug single-room affairs to spacious two bedrooms.

They’re all scattered amongst the tree-filled property’s sycamores and redwoods, so traipsing to your room feels like a walk in the forest. Inside, the aesthetic is a study in NorCal quiet luxury, with plenty of smooth blonde wood, layered textiles, and eclectic furniture pieces, plus Parachute linens and Le Labo bath goodies.

More adventurous guests will appreciate the smartly furnished glamping tents, situated in Dawn Ranch’s 120-year-old apple tree orchard. The walls may be canvas, but the beds feature the same Bear hybrid mattresses as those in Dawn Ranch’s more conventional rooms. You will, however, have to share a bathhouse—albeit an extremely nice one—with your fellower glampers.

No matter where you sleep, make sure you lay eyes on the resort’s namesake, a 70-year-old pair of rare dawn redwoods located near the pool on the main campus.

The restaurants and dining experience

The Lodge at Dawn Ranch, which houses the hotel’s main dining, bar, and lounge areas, manages a laid-back vibe that nonetheless feels rarefied and celebratory, with plush mauve-colored banquettes and dim romantic lighting.

But food is the real draw: Co-executive chefs (and husband-and-wife team) Ignacio “Nacho” Zuzulich and Juliana Thorpe center a nine-course, $155 tasting menu informed both by their respective Argentinian and Brazilian backgrounds and their experience cooking in lauded kitchens from Mugaritz in Spain to Napa Valley’s Meadowood resort. A truncated version of the tasting menu is served at the bar for $90.

Seasonal Golden State ingredients take top billing. On a recent visit, corn was a standout, taking the form of a delicate tostada set atop a fire-roasted corn custard. Festooned with the marigold-like flowering herb huacatay, it conveyed an impossibly large, flawless lobe of Santa Barbara uni.

In the morning, don’t skip breakfast at the Lodge, which is best taken on the sprawling outside deck. Soft scrambled eggs with avocado and furikake on homemade brioche are straightforward but deeply effective, while the cinnamon rolls glossed in cream cheese frosting are the perfect excuse to eat dessert before noon.

Rachel Tepper Paley

Rachel Tepper Paley

The inside scoop

When drinking, whether in the dining room or bar, vino is the move. This is wine country, after all. The handwritten “Sommelier’s Notebook” dispenses with formality, breaking wines into playful categories like “The Wild Ones,” “Extrovert Whites,” and “Quiet Elegance.” You’ll have plenty of fun ordering by the bottle or glass; if you’re after just a taste, some offerings are available in one-ounce pours.

But for the deep-pocketed, the $400 Decades Wine Pairing is a voyage through time and space, guiding you through wines bottled across generations. The offerings frequently shift, but this past summer, the oldest pour was an intensely molasses-forward D'Oliveiras Verdelho Madeira, first put under cork in 1891.

With its decadent syrup-like texture and vibrant acidity, the Madeira made for a complex complement to the tasting menu’s show-stopping dessert course, which presented local peaches in three manners: a quenelle of peach sorbet; a crystal cupful of peach nectar; and a tart of roasted peach jam and white chocolate ganache, topped with intricately woven, paper-thin peach slivers and served alongside a peach sabayon.

Best of all, returning to my cottage after dinner required only a brief, tipsy walk through the redwoods, the stars lighting my way.

Rachel Tepper Paley

This excerpt was originally published in Pre Shift, our newsletter for the hospitality industry. Subscribe for more first-person accounts, advice, and interviews.

Now Open is a yearlong series celebrating some of 2026’s most exciting new restaurants. Throughout the year, we’ll check in with teams in Chicago, New York City, and Washington, D.C., to hear what it’s really like behind the scenes of a buzzy opening. Then, we’ll host exclusive meals at these restaurants as part of Dinner Party, presented by Capital One. Read along for challenges, candid reflections, and advice from the proprietors behind some of the country’s hottest new openings.

Zubair Mohajir is one of Chicago’s most prolific new chefs and restaurateurs, behind such openings as Lilac Tiger, Mariela, Mirra, Sarima, and most recently, Muhājir, a restaurant that traces historical spice routes to tell the story of global migration. I talked to Mohajir about how the opening is going, how he thinks about collaboration across his different projects, and why Muhājir is finally the restaurant that feels like home.

Pre Shift: What did you want to explore with Muhājir that you hadn’t been able to do yet with your previous restaurants?

Zubair Mohajir: Muhājir is such a personal story for me, because my last name is Mohajir, and the meaning of “muhājir” in Arabic and Urdu is “one who migrates.” When the partition [of India and Pakistan] happened, the Muslims that were moved from India to Pakistan were named Muhājirs because they were migrated. In my family, we always wondered why that was our last name. When I started cooking [after working in finance], it really started to settle in. Our late maternal grandfather was obsessed with mapping where this family name came from. It comes from Southern Basra, Iraq, and that was so mind-blowing for me because it’s one of the biggest spice roads.

At Coach House for the past five years, I’ve been exploring ancient recipes in southern Spain and southern Portugal. [They] bring in pre-Crusade Muslim, Christian, Jewish [influences] that are also affected by the Southeast Asian traders coming on the spice road that shoots through the Mediterranean and hits North Africa and the Iberian Peninsula. I’m just obsessed with history and it started to become very evident for me that I really wanted to feed people, but with the context of where the food came from.

At Muhājir, it’s all about riding the spice road that runs from Portugal through the Mediterranean, through the Levantine [region], and then hits out of Basra, Iraq, into the Persian Gulf, and the first landmass it comes across is southern India, where I’m from. We’re all muhājirs — you know, all of our families came from somewhere, and that really has been the driving force for me.

Why did you decide to build the restaurant around live fire?

I’d never cooked on live fire, but we’re cooks, and it was going back to core things. I remember growing up in my grandmother’s house back home in India, and it’s not like there were gas stoves everywhere. When I decided that I was going to do Muhājir, it became so obvious to me that it couldn’t just be a sauté pan on a stove. The story that we wanted to tell had to be told through wood fire.

Is there a dish that feels especially representative of Muhājir?

We do a duck that is inspired by a 927-year-old recipe we found from southern Spain that is influenced by Roman garums, Muslim origins, and Jewish origins. We do this duck “experience,” where we take a whole duck, butcher it, and have the crown dry-aging for seven days. We take the wings and make a jus [and] take the legs and make a confit. We blast that duck crown over the fire when we start service every day, and then it gets finished in the brasa. If you’re sitting in the restaurant, you can see the ducks hanging over the fire.

When we present it, we have this beautiful ornate Turkish platter. There’s black raspberry achaar, the duck jus in a saucier, the duck rice next to it, the duck skin cut in these beautiful medallions on top almost like duck chicharrón, and then we’re also presenting the duck breast itself that has a very crispy skin. The top of that duck breast is the spice mix from that exact recipe that’s more than 900 years old, with cumin, coriander, cardamom, toasted pine nuts, red wine vinegar, and fish sauce. It’s a story of cross-cultural collaboration.

You have a bar called Bobo behind the restaurant. How do the two spaces complement each other?

Bobo’s really inspired by Jacob Dela Cruz, who’s my partner here. We built Sarima together, and it became very important to me to highlight his upbringing and his background as well. He was one who said, “You should name the restaurant Muhājir.” His point was that we’re all immigrants. I was like, “That’s such a simple statement, but such a profound statement.” It was kind of vice versa when we were talking about the bar: Jacob’s father is an amazing person and his name is Bho, and “bobo” in Tagalog means “silly” or “stupid,” as a term of endearment. We always say that as Spice Road-driven and transformative the food experience at Muhājir is, we still like to have fun.

If people are early for their reservation, we take them back to Bobo, or they stop by after dinner. You can’t get to Bobo without walking through the restaurant, so the spaces contribute to each other. If you came to Bobo, you might be like, “I want to eat there.” And if you come straight to Muhājir and see people walking back constantly, you might be like, “What’s happening back there?”

What has it been like to run Muhājir so far?

I wouldn’t say it’s easier [than my other restaurants], but now I don’t freak out. I’ve created a methodical way of approaching issues or problems head-on and figuring it out as a group or with the people that support us. We don’t have investors who are private equity firms; our investors are our guests. When it comes to managing expectations and navigating obstacles, you get better with repetition.

I’m living a dream. Sometimes, when you’re building restaurants with others, you’re not necessarily in the kitchen. [At Mirra, I] was like, “I’m helping create and build this concept, but that’s [chef Rishi Kumar’s] kitchen to run.” Here, it’s the home that I’ve been yearning for and working toward my whole career. I plan to be old in this place. Things have been so crazy and wild and amazing, but slowly, every day, I sit more and more in that moment where I’m like, “This is home.”

This interview has been edited and condensed.

items.text:
Home to some 3.5 million people, Madrid is the capital of Spain and the country’s largest city. Though it’s somewhat sprawling, the city boasts stunning architecture, incredible food, and an energetic nightlife that stretches until dawn. Over 10 million people visit the city each year, and the minute you step out to explore, you’ll understand why Madrid is one of Europe’s top destinations.


Like Barcelona, Madrid is a city that starts late and goes slow. It’s a city for night owls, where dinner starts late and the parties even later. But if you can embrace the laid-back pace of life, the slow meals, and the late-night vibes, you’ll have a more authentic visit and uncover the true beating heart of the city’s culture.


I love all my visits to Madrid. I’ve been a few times over the years and the city never ceases to amaze me. The food, the energy, the art (so much art!). Madrid is just cool.


Being such a big city, I know it can be easy to feel lost. Where do you start with what you want to do? Where do you go? It took me a few visits to figure it out.


In this post, I’ll help you plan an epic five-day visit to Madrid that will ensure you not only see the main sights but that you also get off the beaten path and see just what makes Madrid so popular — and all without breaking the bank either!

Day 1: Immersion in the Art Walk


This first day focuses on a prestigious area designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2021. There are over 40 monuments and over 40 buildings on the site. It’s easily one of the most picturesque and historic areas of the city.


The route begins at the Prado Museum, one of the best museums on the planet. Here you’ll find works from El Greco, Velázquez, and Goya, as well as many other masters (such as Rubens, Botticelli, and Caravaggio to name a few). If you only visit one museum in Madrid, this is the one. It’s incredible and worth taking the time to explore. It’s one of the biggest museums in the world, too. Make sure you spend a few hours here at a minimum.


Just a 10-minute walk along the Paseo del Prado, the journey continues at the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, a private collection spanning from the Renaissance to Pop Art, and culminates at the Reina Sofía Museum. The Reina Sofía National Art Center offers a fantastic collection of modern art. Works by masters like Picasso, Miró, Kandinsky, Dalí, and Bacon can all be found here. The centerpiece is Picasso’s famous Guernica, a 1937 oil painting considered the most moving anti-war painting in the world. While I don’t love modern art, even I enjoyed this museum.


After museum hopping, it’s time to dive into Madrid’s culinary scene. Try Taberna La Fragua de Vulcano for a rustic atmosphere perfect for sampling cocido madrileño. If you are near the Reina Sofía Museum, don’t miss the vibrant garden terrace at Arzábal, renowned for having some of the best croquetas in the city. Finally, for a unique setting, Bodega de los Secretos lets you dine in restored 17th-century wine caves, making it the most atmospheric choice near the Prado Museum.


After a late lunch, spend some time exploring Madrid’s unique ‘House Museums. These are former private palaces that preserve the intimate atmosphere of their original owners. The crown jewel of this collection is the Sorolla Museum, the sun-drenched former residence of ‘the painter of light.’ Following a major architectural renovation, this underrated museum is set to reopen its doors in 2026, offering a refreshed look at its stunning gardens and Mediterranean canvases.


Or if you want something else, there is also the nearby Museum of Romanticism, where you can enjoy a coffee in its secret garden, or visit the Lázaro Galdiano Museum to marvel at a private collection of Goya, Murillo, Velázquez, El Greco, or Bosch housed in a magnificent neo-Renaissance mansion.


In the evening, enjoy some food and relaxation.


Day 2: The Grandeur of the Historic Center


The second day delves into the medieval and Renaissance layout of the city, famously known as Habsburg Madrid (Madrid de los Austrias). The central hub is Puerta del Sol, where a photo at Kilometer Zero and the Bear and the Strawberry Tree statue are mandatory for a traveler’s geographic check-in. Kilometer Zero is the official starting point of all the highways and railways in the country, making this effectively the center of the entire country. There’s a small plaque you can snap a photo of.


Nearby is the Bear and the Strawberry Tree statue (El Oso y el Madroño). The statue shows a bear reaching up to eat fruit from a madroño tree, symbols which come from Madrid’s coat of arms (the bear represents the city and the tree represents the land and nature surrounding it that has helped make it prosper).


From here, walk toward the iconic Plaza Mayor, highlighting its porticoed architecture and the Casa de la Panadería. Plaza Mayor once hosted bullfights, markets, symphonies, tournaments, and even executions. Now it’s ringed with tourist shops, cafés, and restaurants. It’s a good place from which to indulge in some people-watching, offers some good (though overpriced) bars, and occasionally has concerts and events.


For a true “Local Life” experience, stop for a calamari sandwich in the nearby alleys. Your taste buds will thank you.


After a relaxing lunch and some people watching, head to the Royal Palace of Madrid. The largest palace in Western Europe, the Baroque-style palace was built in the 18th century and is home to over 3,400 lavishly decorated rooms. It was originally built on a former 9th-century Muslim fort and today functions much like an art museum with numerous works, including pieces by Caravaggio, Juan de Flandes, and Francisco Goya. Though it’s the official residence of the royal family, they don’t actually live here anymore, and the palace is only used for official state functions. You can walk through the palace (both self-guided and guided tours are available), starting at the grand stairway, and wander through lavishly decorated staterooms. There’s also the Royal Armory, which houses a collection of medieval weapons and armor.


To end the day, head to the Almudena Cathedral. Unlike many of the famous medieval churches in Europe, this one was constructed in the late 19th century. It was finally completed in 1993 and was consecrated by Pope John Paul II. While the exterior has a Neo-Classical design (to match the nearby palace), the cathedral also has a Neo-Romanesque crypt with over 400 columns that you can explore. Be sure to head up to the dome for stunning views out over the city.


Day 3: Culinary Discovery


Madrid is a paradise for foodies. It’s one of the reasons I keep coming back. While there are plenty of food tours to take in Madrid, I suggest heading off on your own to explore. Begin at the city’s iconic gastronomic markets. The glass-walled Mercado de San Miguel is a must for gourmet tapas near Plaza Mayor. It’s popular with the after-work crowd and is a place I usually visit a few times on my trips. Additionally, local favorites like Mercado de San Antón in Chueca and Mercado de Vallehermoso offer a deeper dive into regional flavors. Just make sure to bring an appetite.


If you do want to take a food tour, consider doing a food tour. This post has more of my suggestions.


For dinner, head to Sobrino de Botín, officially recognized by the Guinness World Records as the world’s oldest restaurant. It was actually a favorite of Ernest Hemingway during his time in Madrid. For a more casual vibe, go ‘tapas crawling’ through the historic streets of La Latina or Barrio de las Letras.


As the sun sets, head to the Gran Vía to experience Madrid’s world-class rooftop culture. Venues like The Roof at Picalagartos or RIU, 360º sky bar offer signature cocktails and dinner with breathtaking 360-degree views of the skyline.


For those who don’t eat meat, Madrid has actually evolved into one of Europe’s best veg hubs, boasting a vibrant vegetarian and vegan scene in neighborhoods like Malasaña, where plant-based versions of traditional Spanish dishes are now a staple of the city’s diverse culinary identity.


Day 4: UNESCO World Heritage Wonders


Madrid is the only European capital where nature, science, and royal history converge in a UNESCO World Heritage oasis known as the ‘Paisaje de la Luz‘ (Landscape of Light). But this prestigious area, encompassing the iconic El Retiro Park and the Paseo del Prado, is just the beginning of Spain’s monumental legacy. For more UNESCO wonders, take a day trip out of the city.


One popular destination worth visiting is the Monastery of San Lorenzo de El Escorial, a sprawling imperial masterpiece recognized by UNESCO for its historical significance. El Escorial is located just one hour from the city by car and was commissioned by Philip II in the 16th century. It’s a massive palatial complex that includes a monastery, library, palace, basilica, and tomb for Spanish monarchs. Yet as massive as it is, it feels more austere than other palatial complexes, likely owing to its granite walls and symmetrical layout.


Another option for a day trip is the Royal Palace and Gardens of Aranjuez, a World Heritage Cultural Landscape that rivals the beauty of Versailles. Located just one hour south of the city, this was originally a hunting lodge, also commissioned in the 16th century by Philip II. It’s a blend of Renaissance and Baroque styles, with lavish rooms filled with tapestries, porcelain, and ornate decorations. There is lots of greenery and gardens here, which is partly why the royal family used this as their spring residence.


Lastly, there’s the historic university city of Alcalá de Henares, the birthplace of Spanish novelist, poet, and playwright Cervantes (he wrote Don Quixote). Just 45 minutes away by car, it also holds its own UNESCO World Heritage status, offering a perfectly preserved look into the Spanish Golden Age (1492–1659).


Day 5: Off-the-Beaten-Path Treasures


On your last day, it’s time to get further off the beaten path. Step back into the Golden Age at the Monastery of Las Descalzas Reales and the nearby Royal Monastery of La Encarnación, two hidden palaces that house breathtaking royal art collections behind their cloistered walls.


The Monastery of Las Descalzas Reales is a convent founded in 1559 by Joanna of Austria (sister of Philip II). The name “Descalzas Reales” (which means “Royal Barefoot Ladies”) refers to the Order of Saint Clare nuns who lived here in relative austerity. What makes this monastery unique is that many aristocratic women took refuge here, often bringing their artworks and other valuables. Over the years, this turned the convent into a veritable treasure trove of art.


The Royal Monastery of La Encarnación was founded in 1611 by the wife of Philip III, Margaret of Austria. It was a royal convent, meaning it had the direct support of the monarchy. While the exterior has an austere Baroque style, the interior is quite lavish, with ornate chapels, colorful frescoes, and lots of religious sculptures and paintings. It’s also home to several notable relics, including a vial said to contain the blood of Saint Januarius. While tours are available, it’s still an active convent so parts are not open to the public (which, honestly, makes it all the more interesting to see).


To end your day with a local touch, head to the vast Casa de Campo park. This is the largest public park in the city, created in 1931. It covers a whopping 17 square kilometers (6.5 square miles) and includes an artificial lake, lots of paths, a zoo, and even an amusement park. Here, you can enjoy a scenic lunch or dinner at one of the lakeside terraces, offering an unrivaled view of the Royal Palace and Almudena Cathedral across the skyline. It’s the perfect place to end your trip.


***


While Barcelona tends to get more attention, I think Madrid is one of the best cities in Europe. It boasts a mouthwatering culinary scene, a raucous nightlife, and tons of things to see and do — no matter your interest or budget. I’ve been visiting the city for almost two decades and never get tired of the tapas, architecture, and history. The city just packs so much in and there really is something for everyone here. By following the itinerary above, you’ll see all the main sights while also getting off the beaten path in Spain’s historic capital.

算力硬件和芯片股反弹，光模块、光通信、芯片股等盘中一度拉升，华尔街见闻文章写道，周二美股超微电脑业绩远超预期，“AI交易”应声反弹，“服务器巨头”戴尔、慧与科技盘后大涨，AI云计算CoreWeave亦大涨。亚太股市韩国KOSPI指数涨超3%，芯片巨头三星电子、SK海力士均涨6%。宁德时代AH股大幅下跌，财报显示，公司第三季度净利润同比增长14.54%；单季度综合毛利率降至20.69%，连续两个季度回落。

10月21日，A股三大指数高开低走、全天震荡下行，创业板指尾盘一度跌超2%、最终失守2700点并创阶段新低，早盘一度涨近1%。宁德时代因三季报利润失速叠加外资密集下调评级，全天下跌12.03%、创历史最大单日跌幅，单日蒸发市值逾千亿，重创电池产业链与创业板指。AI硬件以及芯片半导体反弹，光通信、光模块、存储芯片等概念股拉升。

港股高开低走，恒指、恒科指双双下跌，恒科指跌超1%，盘初恒科指曾涨超1%，权重科网股多数下跌，芯片股反弹，澜起科技、兆易创新等涨幅居前。宁德时代港股同样大跌11%。债市方面，国债期货全线下跌。商品方面，国内商品期货涨跌互现。

A股：截至收盘，沪指跌0.60%，深成指跌0.82%，创业板指跌1.62%。

盘面上，个股跌多涨少，沪深京三市超3300股飘绿，今日成交1.44万亿。沪深两市成交额1.43万亿，较上一个交易日缩量268亿。板块方面，新能源汽车产业链、家电、白酒、煤炭、电信、金融板块调整。农业、光通信、存储板块走强。

港股：截至发稿，恒指跌0.35%，恒科指跌0.75%。

盘面上，宁德时代绩后跌超11%，新能源汽车股整体低迷。腾讯控股、中国移动等权重股走软；中际旭创盘中再创新低。

债市：国债期货全线下跌，截至收盘，30年期主力合约跌0.38%，10年期主力合约跌0.10%，5年期主力合约跌0.06%，2年期主力合约跌0.01%。

商品：国内商品期货涨跌参半，截至收盘，基本金属涨幅居前，镍涨3.05%；农副产品多数上涨，红枣涨2.23%；黑色系多数上涨，不锈钢涨2.02%；航运期货跌幅居前，集运指数(欧线)跌7.95%；新能源材料全部下跌，碳酸锂跌4.71%；贵金属多数下跌，钯跌2.90%；能源品全部下跌，燃油跌2.29%；非金属建材涨跌参半，玻璃跌1.29%；油脂油料多数下跌，豆粕跌1.04%；化工品多数下跌，20号胶跌0.74%。

尾盘宽基ETF放量

创业板ETF易方达最后10分钟成交超20亿元，约占全天成交额的五分之一。科创50ETF华夏、沪深300ETF华泰柏瑞均在最后10分钟放量拉升。其中，沪深300ETF华泰柏瑞最后10分钟成交近28亿元，接近全天成交额的一半。

据上证报，近期，宽基ETF成交频放量。其中，10月20日，科创50ETF华夏、创业板ETF易方达、上证50ETF华夏均出现异动拉升。

据Choice测算，当日上证50ETF华夏净流入44.19亿元、科创50ETF华夏净流入29.98亿元、创业板ETF易方达净流入16.74亿元。

此轮资金大规模净流入始于9月28日。据Choice测算，9月28日以来，截至10月20日，12个交易日时间，股票型ETF净流入1973.06亿元。从资金流向看，宽基ETF是资金重要加仓方向。

具体来看，科创50ETF华夏净流入279.02亿元，沪深300ETF华泰柏瑞净流入233.79亿元，沪深300ETF易方达净流入216.18亿元，创业板ETF易方达净流入214.56亿元，上证50ETF华夏净流入也超过110亿元。

中信建投认为，9月28日以来，增量资金主要集中于核心宽基的少数产品，部分产品的交易在尾盘集中放量，且流入区间伴随着市场的持续调整，并在多个交易日延续这一趋势，体现出较强的大机构资金入场特征。

宁德时代暴跌12.03%创历史最大单日跌幅，电池产业链集体重挫

当日盘面最大的拖累来自电池产业链，核心是万亿权重股宁德时代的"失速"。截至收盘，宁德时代报227.90元、跌12.03%，创历史最大单日跌幅，股价自2026年5月7日创出的历史高点回落超50%（"腰斩"）。

时代万恒跌停，上海洗霸跌停，蔚蓝锂芯、先导智能跌超9%，科达利、紫竹高科、尚太科技、盟固利跌超7%，恩捷股份、亿纬锂能、鹏辉能源跌超4%。

宁德时代暴跌的催化是"三季报利润失速+外资评级下调"的共振。

业绩层面，10月20日晚间披露的三季报显示，公司前三季度营收4421.37亿元、同比增长56.19%，归母净利润645.30亿元、同比增长31.60%（前三季日均净赚约2.4亿元）；单季看，第三季度营收1652.21亿元、同比增长58.58%，归母净利润212.46亿元、同比增长14.54%，但环比第二季度的225.46亿元下降5.77%，单季度综合毛利率降至20.69%、连续两个季度回落。

此外，第三季度研发投入达71.4亿元、同比增长43.6%，资产减值损失约18.9亿元（主要由锂价波动引发的库存计提导致），前三季度经营活动现金流量净额约616.25亿元、同比下降23.6%。

市场将利润增速明显低于营收增速归因于三方面：一是三季度低附加值、结构相对简单的产品占比提升，高毛利复杂系统产品占比下降（管理层认为具偶发性）；二是9月起恢复征收的2%电池消费税在尚未与客户谈妥分摊方案前暂由公司承担；三是出口增值税退税率下调（9%降至6%）影响在三季度完整体现，叠加碳酸锂价格波动导致的存货减值。

不过出货量基本盘仍强，第三季度电池总出货量超260GWh、同比增长约60%，其中动力电池约199GWh、同比增长50%，储能电池约66GWh、同比翻倍。

近期部分投资者对明年新能源行业需求有些担心。对此，宁德时代最新回应称，从公司角度看，2027年行业需求依旧可以期待。国内乘用车方面，尽管今年乘用车整体销量有所下降，但可以看到电动化率在快速提升，并且单车带电量有较快提升，所以国内新能源乘用车动力电池的增速依然实现了正增长。整体而言，全球动力及储能电池的市场需求可能没有市场预期的那么悲观，仍有不错的增长潜力。

评级层面，多家外资机构密集下调评级与目标价。花旗将宁德时代A股目标价从500元下调至479元、H股目标价从765港元下调至732港元，理由是三季度净利润不及预期（毛利率低于预期、费用及资产减值损失增加），并将2026—2028年盈利预期分别下调9%、14%、15%至860亿、1030亿、1220亿元，同时预计在所有负面消息被消化后，股价跑赢的下一个窗口期可能是2027年第一季度。

摩根大通将H股评级下调至"中性"、目标价从725港元大幅下调至500港元，A股维持"增持"评级并下调盈利预测，同时维持宁德时代A股为其所覆盖电池股中唯一评级"增持"的股份；该行表示日益担忧动力电池行业盈利能力恶化的速度快于预期，电池消费税、出口退税率下调及贸易壁垒增加等多重因素叠加，整个电动汽车产业链的利润正在经历更广泛的重新分配，但宁德时代可能最先受到冲击、最终或成为较大赢家。

高盛此前已将H股目标价下调至859港元、维持"买入"评级。针对市场担忧，宁德时代在业绩说明会上回应称"市场需求没有那么悲观"，一个季度的产品结构波动不代表长期方向。

数据要素：国家数据集团成立，三维天地、慧辰股份20CM涨停

三维天地20CM涨停、慧辰股份20CM涨停、利亚德20CM涨停；南威软件4天3板、星光股份4天3板，海量数据涨停、太极股份涨停、天威视讯涨停，深桑达A涨4.10%，数字认证、久远银海、志晟信息、海天瑞声等跟涨。

催化逻辑链清晰且重磅：

其一，国家数据集团正式成立。据新华社报道，10月20日，国家数据集团有限公司在河北雄安新区成立，以数据资源开发利用为主责主业，位列国务院国资委央企名录第28位，此次列入后国资委监管的中央企业由99家增至100家。

集团由国务院、河北雄安新区管理委员会、中国电信、中国联通、中国移动、国家电网、南方电网共同出资组建，目标是成为数据要素服务国家队、数据基础设施互联互通引领者、国家数据科技创新战略力量，未来将聚焦为人工智能产业提供高质量数据集和语料库、推动"人工智能+"行动落地等重点工作。

其二，专家解读强化政策预期。国家数据专家咨询委员会委员张向宏表示，集团以市场化、专业化为导向，将承担开发、整合和运营国家级数据资源的重任，推动数据跨行业、跨区域流动与共享，大幅提升数据资源配置效率，破除"数据孤岛"，有助于加快构建全国一体化数据市场；从国际看，国家层面成立数据集团属全球先行先试，将有效提升我国在全球数据资源竞争中的地位。

其三，产业数据提供景气佐证。数据显示，截至2026年6月底，全国高质量数据集达12万个、总量超1565PB，较一季度末增长超60%；日均词元调用量达140万亿，半年提升超40%。

国泰海通证券指出，过去公共数据开放主要服务政务效率，如今大模型与具身智能把高质量数据变成AI的"燃料"，叠加"为优质数据付费"与词元交易的定价探索，数据正从"开放共享"走向"定价交易"，归集、标注治理、登记流通、场景开发各环节需求有望同步扩容，2026年为"数据要素价值释放年"，国家队入场叠加AI数据需求，持续看好数据要素产业链，建议关注训练数据服务、垂直产业数据和公共数据运营方向。

中泰证券表示，国家数据集团的成立标志着数据要素市场化改革进入深水区，将通过顶层设计推动数据资源的整合与流通，催动数据要素的资产化、资本化进展加速。

中信建投认为，9月28日以来，增量资金主要集中于核心宽基的少数产品，部分产品的交易在尾盘集中放量，且流入区间伴随着市场的持续调整，并在多个交易日延续这一趋势，体现出较强的大机构资金入场特征。
宁德时代暴跌12.03%创历史最大单日跌幅，电池产业链集体重挫
当日盘面最大的拖累来自电池产业链，核心是万亿权重股宁德时代的"失速"。截至收盘，宁德时代报227.90元、跌12.03%，创历史最大单日跌幅，股价自2026年5月7日创出的历史高点回落超50%（"腰斩"）。
https://wpimg-wscn.awtmt.com/4bbf7706-fca5-47da-a980-39a17b97c1f7.png?imageView2/1/w/110/h/82
https://wpimg-wscn.awtmt.com/f3361a82-1228-445a-a48a-f2c0c3d48ff7.png?imageView2/2/w/680
时代万恒跌停，上海洗霸跌停，蔚蓝锂芯、先导智能跌超9%，科达利、紫竹高科、尚太科技、盟固利跌超7%，恩捷股份、亿纬锂能、鹏辉能源跌超4%。
https://wpimg-wscn.awtmt.com/bc86cca2-c7a6-4ee5-a368-6a5e04e2ef2f.png?imageView2/2/w/680
宁德时代暴跌的催化是"三季报利润失速+外资评级下调"的共振。
业绩层面，10月20日晚间披露的三季报显示，公司前三季度营收4421.37亿元、同比增长56.19%，归母净利润645.30亿元、同比增长31.60%（前三季日均净赚约2.4亿元）；单季看，第三季度营收1652.21亿元、同比增长58.58%，归母净利润212.46亿元、同比增长14.54%，但环比第二季度的225.46亿元下降5.77%，单季度综合毛利率降至20.69%、连续两个季度回落。
此外，第三季度研发投入达71.4亿元、同比增长43.6%，资产减值损失约18.9亿元（主要由锂价波动引发的库存计提导致），前三季度经营活动现金流量净额约616.25亿元、同比下降23.6%。
市场将利润增速明显低于营收增速归因于三方面：一是三季度低附加值、结构相对简单的产品占比提升，高毛利复杂系统产品占比下降（管理层认为具偶发性）；二是9月起恢复征收的2%电池消费税在尚未与客户谈妥分摊方案前暂由公司承担；三是出口增值税退税率下调（9%降至6%）影响在三季度完整体现，叠加碳酸锂价格波动导致的存货减值。
不过出货量基本盘仍强，第三季度电池总出货量超260GWh、同比增长约60%，其中动力电池约199GWh、同比增长50%，储能电池约66GWh、同比翻倍。
近期部分投资者对明年新能源行业需求有些担心。对此，宁德时代最新回应称，从公司角度看，2027年行业需求依旧可以期待。国内乘用车方面，尽管今年乘用车整体销量有所下降，但可以看到电动化率在快速提升，并且单车带电量有较快提升，所以国内新能源乘用车动力电池的增速依然实现了正增长。整体而言，全球动力及储能电池的市场需求可能没有市场预期的那么悲观，仍有不错的增长潜力。
https://wpimg-wscn.awtmt.com/aee32fb7-2963-4d47-900c-ab5c85c421c6.png?imageView2/1/w/110/h/82
评级层面，多家外资机构密集下调评级与目标价。花旗将宁德时代A股目标价从500元下调至479元、H股目标价从765港元下调至732港元，理由是三季度净利润不及预期（毛利率低于预期、费用及资产减值损失增加），并将2026—2028年盈利预期分别下调9%、14%、15%至860亿、1030亿、1220亿元，同时预计在所有负面消息被消化后，股价跑赢的下一个窗口期可能是2027年第一季度。
摩根大通将H股评级下调至"中性"、目标价从725港元大幅下调至500港元，A股维持"增持"评级并下调盈利预测，同时维持宁德时代A股为其所覆盖电池股中唯一评级"增持"的股份；该行表示日益担忧动力电池行业盈利能力恶化的速度快于预期，电池消费税、出口退税率下调及贸易壁垒增加等多重因素叠加，整个电动汽车产业链的利润正在经历更广泛的重新分配，但宁德时代可能最先受到冲击、最终或成为较大赢家。
高盛此前已将H股目标价下调至859港元、维持"买入"评级。针对市场担忧，宁德时代在业绩说明会上回应称"市场需求没有那么悲观"，一个季度的产品结构波动不代表长期方向。
数据要素：国家数据集团成立，三维天地、慧辰股份20CM涨停
三维天地20CM涨停、慧辰股份20CM涨停、利亚德20CM涨停；南威软件4天3板、星光股份4天3板，海量数据涨停、太极股份涨停、天威视讯涨停，深桑达A涨4.10%，数字认证、久远银海、志晟信息、海天瑞声等跟涨。
https://wpimg-wscn.awtmt.com/6b893c25-9bf6-490e-b419-1896b24be8b6.png?imageView2/2/w/680
催化逻辑链清晰且重磅：
https://wpimg-wscn.awtmt.com/20e2ee98-4887-4b66-b8fd-d0e327b8b07c.jpeg?imageView2/1/w/110/h/82
其一，国家数据集团正式成立。据新华社报道，10月20日，国家数据集团有限公司在河北雄安新区成立，以数据资源开发利用为主责主业，位列国务院国资委央企名录第28位，此次列入后国资委监管的中央企业由99家增至100家。
集团由国务院、河北雄安新区管理委员会、中国电信、中国联通、中国移动、国家电网、南方电网共同出资组建，目标是成为数据要素服务国家队、数据基础设施互联互通引领者、国家数据科技创新战略力量，未来将聚焦为人工智能产业提供高质量数据集和语料库、推动"人工智能+"行动落地等重点工作。
其二，专家解读强化政策预期。国家数据专家咨询委员会委员张向宏表示，集团以市场化、专业化为导向，将承担开发、整合和运营国家级数据资源的重任，推动数据跨行业、跨区域流动与共享，大幅提升数据资源配置效率，破除"数据孤岛"，有助于加快构建全国一体化数据市场；从国际看，国家层面成立数据集团属全球先行先试，将有效提升我国在全球数据资源竞争中的地位。
其三，产业数据提供景气佐证。数据显示，截至2026年6月底，全国高质量数据集达12万个、总量超1565PB，较一季度末增长超60%；日均词元调用量达140万亿，半年提升超40%。
国泰海通证券指出，过去公共数据开放主要服务政务效率，如今大模型与具身智能把高质量数据变成AI的"燃料"，叠加"为优质数据付费"与词元交易的定价探索，数据正从"开放共享"走向"定价交易"，归集、标注治理、登记流通、场景开发各环节需求有望同步扩容，2026年为"数据要素价值释放年"，国家队入场叠加AI数据需求，持续看好数据要素产业链，建议关注训练数据服务、垂直产业数据和公共数据运营方向。
中泰证券表示，国家数据集团的成立标志着数据要素市场化改革进入深水区，将通过顶层设计推动数据资源的整合与流通，催动数据要素的资产化、资本化进展加速。

items.text:
SpaceX强劲季报重燃市场对人工智能投资前景的信心，美股期货随之走高，科技股领涨。


标普500期货上涨0.2%，纳斯达克100期货上涨0.7%。SpaceX涨约9%，AI业务收入同比暴增830%并首次成为最大收入来源，净利润超预期2.3倍，提振市场情绪。与此同时，超微电脑（Super Micro Computer）发布亮眼初步季报，盘前涨约15%，进一步强化了AI需求持续强劲的市场叙事。


然而，利好情绪受到一定抑制。油价再度走高，布伦特原油向每桶110美元逼近，霍尔木兹海峡附近的船只遭受袭击威胁供应，同时美国原油库存数据显示库存下降490万桶。美债收益率及美元走势变化不大。奈飞（Netflix）则因四季度营收指引及广告收入双双不及预期，盘前跌约6%，成为当日主要拖累。


BNP Paribas Wealth Management Germany的Stephan Kemper表示："投资者在情绪上天生具有两极性。SpaceX和超微电脑所展示的强劲数据与积极指引，正是市场目前所需要的良药。"


标普500期货上涨0.2%，纳斯达克100期货上涨0.7%。SpaceX涨约9%，超微电脑涨约15%，奈飞跌约6%


欧元下跌0.1%，报1.1224美元


美国10年期国债收益率变化不大，为5.11%


德国十年期收益率变化不大，为3.40%


布伦特原油上涨0.9%，至每桶109.72美元


现货黄金下跌0.1%，报每盎司4,120.68美元

SpaceX季报引爆AI交易

SpaceX三季度营收145.8亿美元，同比增长161%，AI业务收入同比暴增830%，首次超越其他业务成为公司最大单一收入来源，净利润超出市场预期2.3倍。


据彭博，ING首席投资策略师Simon Wiersma表示："SpaceX提供了市场正在寻找的答案——AI相关需求依然真实存在。这不仅提振了市场对SpaceX本身的信心，也改善了对整个AI生态系统的情绪。"


此外，埃隆·马斯克就SpaceX与特斯拉潜在合并表态支持，进一步推动SpaceX股价上行。


Anthropic千亿算力计划助力市场信心修复

SpaceX财报的超预期表现，叠加Anthropic PBC据报道计划未来数年投入高达7500亿美元用于算力建设，共同缓解了近期因估值高企和融资压力引发的市场忧虑。


BNP Paribas Wealth Management Germany的Stephan Kemper表示："投资者在情绪上天生具有两极性。SpaceX和超微电脑所展示的强劲数据与积极指引，正是市场目前所需要的良药。"


本周科技股财报季仍将持续，Meta Platforms与特斯拉将于周三盘后发布财报，市场密切关注AI投入能否继续兑现回报。

超微电脑初步季报超预期，奈飞指引拖累情绪

超微电脑公布第一财季初步业绩，营收超出分析师预期27%，盘前股价随之跳涨约15%，再度印证AI算力基础设施需求旺盛。


与科技硬件板块的强势形成对比，奈飞盘前下跌约6%。公司四季度营收指引与广告收入均低于市场预期，拖累流媒体板块情绪。

欧洲及亚洲市场表现分化

欧洲市场，斯托克600指数小幅上涨，能源和科技板块上涨被消费相关板块的回落所抵消。斯托克50指数开盘涨0.3%，法国CAC 40指数涨0.1%，德国DAX指数基本持平，英国富时100指数跌0.1%。法国10年期国债相对德国同期国债的收益率溢价扩大至逾155个基点。


亚洲市场，区域股市基准指数整体反弹，韩国综合股价指数（Kospi）表现居前。韩国Elice Inc.在经历韩国史上最差IPO首日表现之一后，股价单日反弹30%。

items.title: 中共中央办公厅、国务院办公厅发布关于推动科技创新和产业创新深度融合的意见
items.summary:
10月21日，中共中央办公厅、国务院办公厅对外发布《关于推动科技创新和产业创新深度融合的意见》，要求以发展新质生产力、建设现代化产业体系为目标，以构建企业主导、各主体协同的产学研融通创新体系为重点，推动全链条贯通、全领域覆盖、全要素融通、全方位保障，形成科技创新和产业创新互融共促新格局。

意见围绕促进创新链产业链无缝
items.text:
10月21日，中共中央办公厅、国务院办公厅对外发布《关于推动科技创新和产业创新深度融合的意见》，要求以发展新质生产力、建设现代化产业体系为目标，以构建企业主导、各主体协同的产学研融通创新体系为重点，推动全链条贯通、全领域覆盖、全要素融通、全方位保障，形成科技创新和产业创新互融共促新格局。

意见围绕促进创新链产业链无缝对接、以高质量科技供给支撑现代化产业体系建设、加强企业主导的产学研融通创新、提高创新资源统筹配置效能、营造深度融合的良好生态和拓展深度融合的发展空间6个方面作出具体部署。

中共中央办公厅　国务院办公厅关于推动科技创新和产业创新深度融合的意见

为推动科技创新和产业创新深度融合，经党中央、国务院同意，现提出如下意见。

一、总体要求

坚持以习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想为指导，深入贯彻党的二十大和二十届历次全会精神，认真落实四中全会部署，深入实施创新驱动发展战略，以发展新质生产力、建设现代化产业体系为目标，以构建企业主导、各主体协同的产学研融通创新体系为重点，推动全链条贯通、全领域覆盖、全要素融通、全方位保障，形成科技创新和产业创新互融共促新格局，打通从科技强到产业强、经济强、国家强的通道，为加快高水平科技自立自强、实现高质量发展、建设社会主义现代化强国提供支撑。

工作中要做到：坚持准确把握科技革命和产业变革新趋势新特点，加强系统谋划和一体推进；坚持统筹科技供给和需求牵引，围绕产业链部署创新链，围绕创新链布局产业链；坚持强化企业创新主体地位，完善激励创新的市场机制，推动创新资源向企业集聚；坚持以改革激发创新活力，坚决破除阻碍科技创新和产业创新深度融合发展的思想观念和制度障碍。

二、促进创新链产业链无缝对接

（一）健全创新统筹机制。发挥新型举国体制优势，强化科技创新和产业创新战略规划、重大任务、政策措施的统筹协调。按照“面向世界科技前沿、面向经济主战场、面向国家重大需求、面向人民生命健康”要求，在重点前沿领域统筹科技和产业发展重大政策、重大工程、重大项目。加强科技、产业、金融、教育、人才等政策协同。面向地方、行业开展科技创新和产业创新深度融合监测评估，把科技创新引领产业发展和产业创新水平作为重点内容。

（二）改革任务组织模式。强化国家科技计划项目的产业应用导向，常态化征集企业需求，在指南编制、立项评审、项目验收中，合理增加来自企业和创业投资机构的专家数量，推动科技界、产业界、用户等多方参与。健全企业牵头项目的管理规定，完善“揭榜挂帅”、“业主制”等组织方式和“里程碑”管理、分阶段拨款等资助方式。健全“应用考核技术、市场考核产品”的项目验收机制，加强研发目标和产业化目标一体考核。推动国家重大工程和产业发展专项同步部署科研任务，明确科技创新目标，健全组织实施机制。

（三）畅通科技成果转化途径。健全研用一体的成果转化应用机制，产业应用目标明确的国家科技计划项目，原则上由企业牵头实施并主导成果转化。支持高校、科研院所设立技术转移机构或岗位，强化知识产权、创业孵化、科技金融等专业化服务，通过技术转让、许可、作价投资等方式加快成果应用。深化职务科技成果赋权和资产单列管理改革，鼓励科技成果完成人全过程参与成果转化，引导高校、科研院所按照先使用后付费方式把科技成果许可给中小微企业使用。健全全国一体化技术市场，促进专业化市场化技术转移机构发展，加强技术经理人队伍建设。

（四）强化场景驱动创新。实施新技术新产品新场景应用示范行动，加大场景培育和开放力度。支持地方在政务服务、智慧城市、乡村建设等领域加大应用场景建设和开放力度，加强技术、场景等供需信息汇集发布。强化场景开放协同共享。

三、以高质量科技供给支撑现代化产业体系建设

（五）以关键核心技术突破提升产业链自主可控水平。推动集成电路、工业母机、高端仪器、先进材料、生物制造等重点领域关键核心技术攻关取得决定性突破。深入实施产业基础再造和重大技术装备攻关等工程，聚焦重点领域薄弱环节，强化基础零部件及基础元器件攻关，突破关键基础软件，攻克关键基础材料，加强先进基础工艺和产业技术基础研发。

（六）以原创性颠覆性科技创新培育壮大新兴产业和未来产业。加强基础理论研究和底层技术研发，开展颠覆性技术挖掘甄别，加速科学发现和技术突破。实施产业创新工程，一体推进创新设施建设、技术研究开发、产品迭代升级，加快新能源、新材料、航空航天等战略性新兴产业发展，因地制宜建设各具特色、优势互补的战略性新兴产业集群，着力打造新兴支柱产业。推动低空经济健康有序发展。在量子科技、生物制造、氢能和核聚变能、脑机接口、具身智能、第六代移动通信等前沿领域，探索多元技术路线、典型应用场景、可行商业模式，加快推进前沿技术产业化商业化，培育形成未来产业。

（七）以先进技术改造提升传统产业。深入实施制造业重大技术改造升级和大规模设备更新工程，加速工业互联网创新发展，促进数字经济和实体经济深度融合，推动制造业智能化、绿色化、融合化发展。加强种业、农机装备等科研攻关，加快农业科技成果推广应用。构建全产业链科技服务体系，促进科技服务业优质高效发展。全面实施“人工智能+”行动，推动人工智能全方位赋能千行百业。

四、加强企业主导的产学研融通创新

（八）全面增强企业创新能力。完善企业常态化参与国家科技和产业发展战略、规划、政策制定机制。推动国家自然科学基金试点向民营企业开放，扩大企业创新发展联合基金范围和规模。鼓励国有企业加快建立独立核算、免于增值保值考核、容错纠错的研发准备金制度。鼓励科技型中小企业加大研发投入，提高研发费用加计扣除比例。支持企业牵头建设科技创新平台基地。完善国家重大科技基础设施、大型科研仪器、国家科学数据中心等向企业开放制度。加大各类科技人才计划对企业的支持力度，加强企业博士后工作站建设。

（九）加快培育壮大科技企业。优化科技领军企业培育机制。支持高新技术企业发展。完善科技型中小企业及专精特新“小巨人”企业、制造业单项冠军企业培优机制。加快培育科技型初创企业，完善创业孵化、投融资等服务保障。深化大中小企业、产业链上下游企业融通创新，引导大企业向中小企业开放研发平台、应用场景和供应链，先试首用中小企业创新产品。

（十）加强创新主体协同联动。支持科技领军企业发挥创新链产业链链长作用，牵头组建创新联合体，增强体系化科技攻关能力。国家实验室、国家科研机构、高水平研究型大学加强与科技领军企业合作，注重从产业需求中凝练科学问题，强化战略性前瞻性技术攻关。鼓励企业参与高校、科研院所科研活动和人才培养。支持企业与其他创新主体共建研发机构、共设科研项目。

五、提高创新资源统筹配置效能

（十一）促进科技、产业、金融良性循环。构建与科技企业全生命周期融资需求相适应的科技金融体系。发挥国家创业投资引导基金作用。政府出资的创业投资基金和国有资本创业投资基金强化投早、投小、投长期、投硬科技，健全长周期考核、差异化监管和退出机制。推广“创新积分制”，强化对科技型中小企业创新能力的量化评估。高质量建设债券市场“科技板”。建立科技保险政策体系。

（十二）加强人才协同培养和使用。围绕科技创新、产业发展和国家战略需求协同育人，完善科技、产业部门等多方参与的学科设置调整机制。推广校企联合、工学交替和“双导师制”。完善高校、科研院所科研人员选派挂职、兼职和离岗创业政策，推广科技特派员等模式。支持高校、科研院所聘请企业创新人才担任产业导师、产业教授。支持青年科技人才创新创业，大力培育科技型企业家。

（十三）建设融合创新平台。统筹布局国家新兴产业创新中心、国家产业技术工程化中心、国家技术创新中心、国家制造业创新中心等，强化重点产业关键共性技术供给。建设概念验证中心、中试验证平台，为新技术新产品产业化应用提供服务。支持转制科研院所建设产业技术研究院等共性技术平台。支持地方规范发展新型研发机构，面向产业加强共性技术研发应用。

六、营造深度融合的良好生态

（十四）健全激励创新的市场环境。破除不合理限制创新产品进入市场的制度障碍，在新业态新领域开展放宽市场准入试点，探索开展承诺即入制。加强新技术应用监管，探索“沙盒监管”方式。推动健全人工智能、生物技术等前沿领域法律法规，完善科技伦理制度规范。

（十五）加强知识产权保护、运用和技术标准建设。强化商业秘密和新业态新领域知识产权保护，在产学研合作、科技成果转化中健全利益共享、风险共担机制。全面实施专利开放许可制度。加强国家重大科技项目专利布局。强化国家重大科技项目标准布局，统筹设置标准研究任务和考核目标。全面加强前沿领域国家标准、国际标准研制和预标准研究。推动企业标准、团体标准提质增效。

（十六）完善创新激励和评价政策。健全创新活动全链条政策体系，落实科技创新税收优惠等政策。健全科技成果转化、创业投资等方面尽职免责机制，探索建立负面清单。完善国有企业分类考核评价体系，提高企业与高校、科研院所等联合研发费用视同利润加回的比例。将产学研合作、科技成果转化成效等作为高水平研究型大学、科研院所评估和科研人员评价的重要内容。

七、拓展深度融合的发展空间

（十七）支持地方开展深度融合先行先试。加强对地方科技和产业布局的宏观指导，引导各地立足禀赋优势锻造科技长板和产业特色。加强央地协同，健全中央与地方科技投入共担、重大任务联动实施机制。完善区域创新体系，加强跨区域协同创新。统筹发展各类科技创新和产业创新功能区，推动国家高新技术产业开发区、国家自主创新示范区等开展政策先行先试。推动国际科技创新中心、区域科技创新中心和有条件的地方开展科技创新和产业创新深度融合发展改革试点，深入实施激发产业创新活力专项行动，建设富有活力的创新城市，打造原始创新策源地。

八、加强组织实施

各地区各有关部门要在党中央集中统一领导下，结合实际抓好本意见贯彻落实。（完）

三、以高质量科技供给支撑现代化产业体系建设
（五）以关键核心技术突破提升产业链自主可控水平。推动集成电路、工业母机、高端仪器、先进材料、生物制造等重点领域关键核心技术攻关取得决定性突破。深入实施产业基础再造和重大技术装备攻关等工程，聚焦重点领域薄弱环节，强化基础零部件及基础元器件攻关，突破关键基础软件，攻克关键基础材料，加强先进基础工艺和产业技术基础研发。

（六）以原创性颠覆性科技创新培育壮大新兴产业和未来产业。加强基础理论研究和底层技术研发，开展颠覆性技术挖掘甄别，加速科学发现和技术突破。实施产业创新工程，一体推进创新设施建设、技术研究开发、产品迭代升级，加快新能源、新材料、航空航天等战略性新兴产业发展，因地制宜建设各具特色、优势互补的战略性新兴产业集群，着力打造新兴支柱产业。推动低空经济健康有序发展。在量子科技、生物制造、氢能和核聚变能、脑机接口、具身智能、第六代移动通信等前沿领域，探索多元技术路线、典型应用场景、可行商业模式，加快推进前沿技术产业化商业化，培育形成未来产业。
（七）以先进技术改造提升传统产业。深入实施制造业重大技术改造升级和大规模设备更新工程，加速工业互联网创新发展，促进数字经济和实体经济深度融合，推动制造业智能化、绿色化、融合化发展。加强种业、农机装备等科研攻关，加快农业科技成果推广应用。构建全产业链科技服务体系，促进科技服务业优质高效发展。全面实施“人工智能+”行动，推动人工智能全方位赋能千行百业。
四、加强企业主导的产学研融通创新

（八）全面增强企业创新能力。完善企业常态化参与国家科技和产业发展战略、规划、政策制定机制。推动国家自然科学基金试点向民营企业开放，扩大企业创新发展联合基金范围和规模。鼓励国有企业加快建立独立核算、免于增值保值考核、容错纠错的研发准备金制度。鼓励科技型中小企业加大研发投入，提高研发费用加计扣除比例。支持企业牵头建设科技创新平台基地。完善国家重大科技基础设施、大型科研仪器、国家科学数据中心等向企业开放制度。加大各类科技人才计划对企业的支持力度，加强企业博士后工作站建设。
（九）加快培育壮大科技企业。优化科技领军企业培育机制。支持高新技术企业发展。完善科技型中小企业及专精特新“小巨人”企业、制造业单项冠军企业培优机制。加快培育科技型初创企业，完善创业孵化、投融资等服务保障。深化大中小企业、产业链上下游企业融通创新，引导大企业向中小企业开放研发平台、应用场景和供应链，先试首用中小企业创新产品。
（十）加强创新主体协同联动。支持科技领军企业发挥创新链产业链链长作用，牵头组建创新联合体，增强体系化科技攻关能力。国家实验室、国家科研机构、高水平研究型大学加强与科技领军企业合作，注重从产业需求中凝练科学问题，强化战略性前瞻性技术攻关。鼓励企业参与高校、科研院所科研活动和人才培养。支持企业与其他创新主体共建研发机构、共设科研项目。
五、提高创新资源统筹配置效能
（十一）促进科技、产业、金融良性循环。构建与科技企业全生命周期融资需求相适应的科技金融体系。发挥国家创业投资引导基金作用。政府出资的创业投资基金和国有资本创业投资基金强化投早、投小、投长期、投硬科技，健全长周期考核、差异化监管和退出机制。推广“创新积分制”，强化对科技型中小企业创新能力的量化评估。高质量建设债券市场“科技板”。建立科技保险政策体系。
（十二）加强人才协同培养和使用。围绕科技创新、产业发展和国家战略需求协同育人，完善科技、产业部门等多方参与的学科设置调整机制。推广校企联合、工学交替和“双导师制”。完善高校、科研院所科研人员选派挂职、兼职和离岗创业政策，推广科技特派员等模式。支持高校、科研院所聘请企业创新人才担任产业导师、产业教授。支持青年科技人才创新创业，大力培育科技型企业家。
（十三）建设融合创新平台。统筹布局国家新兴产业创新中心、国家产业技术工程化中心、国家技术创新中心、国家制造业创新中心等，强化重点产业关键共性技术供给。建设概念验证中心、中试验证平台，为新技术新产品产业化应用提供服务。支持转制科研院所建设产业技术研究院等共性技术平台。支持地方规范发展新型研发机构，面向产业加强共性技术研发应用。
六、营造深度融合的良好生态
（十四）健全激励创新的市场环境。破除不合理限制创新产品进入市场的制度障碍，在新业态新领域开展放宽市场准入试点，探索开展承诺即入制。加强新技术应用监管，探索“沙盒监管”方式。推动健全人工智能、生物技术等前沿领域法律法规，完善科技伦理制度规范。
（十五）加强知识产权保护、运用和技术标准建设。强化商业秘密和新业态新领域知识产权保护，在产学研合作、科技成果转化中健全利益共享、风险共担机制。全面实施专利开放许可制度。加强国家重大科技项目专利布局。强化国家重大科技项目标准布局，统筹设置标准研究任务和考核目标。全面加强前沿领域国家标准、国际标准研制和预标准研究。推动企业标准、团体标准提质增效。
（十六）完善创新激励和评价政策。健全创新活动全链条政策体系，落实科技创新税收优惠等政策。健全科技成果转化、创业投资等方面尽职免责机制，探索建立负面清单。完善国有企业分类考核评价体系，提高企业与高校、科研院所等联合研发费用视同利润加回的比例。将产学研合作、科技成果转化成效等作为高水平研究型大学、科研院所评估和科研人员评价的重要内容。
七、拓展深度融合的发展空间

（十七）支持地方开展深度融合先行先试。加强对地方科技和产业布局的宏观指导，引导各地立足禀赋优势锻造科技长板和产业特色。加强央地协同，健全中央与地方科技投入共担、重大任务联动实施机制。完善区域创新体系，加强跨区域协同创新。统筹发展各类科技创新和产业创新功能区，推动国家高新技术产业开发区、国家自主创新示范区等开展政策先行先试。推动国际科技创新中心、区域科技创新中心和有条件的地方开展科技创新和产业创新深度融合发展改革试点，深入实施激发产业创新活力专项行动，建设富有活力的创新城市，打造原始创新策源地。
八、加强组织实施
各地区各有关部门要在党中央集中统一领导下，结合实际抓好本意见贯彻落实。（完）
本文来源：新华社

items.title: SpaceX与特斯拉合并，马斯克在下一盘多大的棋？
items.summary:

马斯克先说自己是在
items.text:
SpaceX交出一份很难再用"火箭公司"概括的成绩单：第三季度，SpaceX营收146亿美元，同比增长161%，净利润44亿美元，超出分析师平均预期逾一倍。


财报电话会上，马斯克确认：SpaceX和特斯拉已分别成立由独立董事组成的特别委员会，讨论可能的合并。两家公司合并估值约3.5万亿美元。


马斯克先说自己是在"雷区里跳踢踏舞"。几秒之后还是给了答案，合并"有很多好处"。Deepwater Asset Management 的 Gene Munster 事后数了数，这句话他讲了大概三遍。


这让一个谈论已久的设想进入了正式评估阶段：彭博指出，特斯拉市值约 1.5 万亿美元，SpaceX 约 2 万亿美元，合在一起 3.5 万亿。


会不会合并，已经不该是问题。巴克莱在 10 月 14 日的报告认为，两家合并的可能性"已经越来越成为共识预期"。股东名册高度重叠，SpaceX 买特斯拉的 Cybertruck，又通过 xAI 买公用事业级储能电池。今年 9 月的 All-In 峰会上，马斯克被问到为什么两家公司要分开，他反问："这么多层面都在合作，谁能想象在如此紧密的合作下会采取什么行动。"


消息传出后，SpaceX盘后涨幅约8%，特斯拉仅涨约1.8%——收购方涨得比被收购方更多。这一差异反映出两类股东截然不同的盘算，也预示着这笔交易在正式落地之前，还有漫长的博弈要走。


SpaceX的AI业务已大到无法当作副业

SpaceX第三季度的收入结构说明了合并讨论为何在此时升温。人工智能及算力业务收入75.6亿美元，较上年同期增长逾九倍，已首次超过Starlink所在的连接业务，季度营业利润从去年同期亏损17亿美元转为盈利4.31亿美元。连接业务营收52.5亿美元，同比增长69%，目前仍贡献更多利润，但增速明显慢于AI业务。相比之下，设计、制造和运营火箭与飞船的传统发射业务营收17.7亿美元，仅增长6%。


增长的另一面是开支。第三季度，SpaceX资本支出接近196亿美元，其中AI及算力业务约164亿美元。前九个月，公司经营现金流约131亿美元，购置物业、厂房及设备支出约481亿美元。单看44亿美元的季度净利润，很容易低估算力设施建设所需的真实资金规模。据报道，SpaceX正在洽谈借款400亿美元用于采购英伟达芯片，CFO Bret Johnsen表示公司会继续举债，"有好几个可用的债务资金池正在谈"，并给出明年一季度总营收最高370亿美元的指引。


SpaceX目前已是Anthropic、Alphabet等公司的主要算力与基础设施供应商，8月还收购了代码编辑工具Cursor。一家收入结构里AI占比最高、正在大举举债买卡的公司，用"火箭公司"来定义已经远远不够。

协同逻辑清晰，但股权合并未必是唯一路径

马斯克列举的合作清单涵盖超级智能软件、芯片设计、Terafab、机器人、轨道数据中心和连接服务。这些项目不断碰到同一批资源：芯片、能源、制造能力，以及能够持续支付建设成本的资本。"简化决策"是合并动机中排名靠前的一项——许多跨公司项目需要两个董事会和两批股东分别点头。


Terafab是其中最具体的节点。按巴克莱测算，特斯拉计划先在奥斯汀建一座约30亿美元的研究设施，随后跟进约168亿美元的生产厂，两家公司很可能共同出资。这里产出的芯片将供给特斯拉自动驾驶汽车和擎天柱机器人，同时也供给SpaceX的AI与轨道数据中心。马斯克此前已明确表示，Terafab的决策需要两家董事会各自审批，"可能要花一阵子"，目标是2028年底量产。


10月15日亮相的新款Roadster搭载了SpaceX开发的冷气推进器，可完成倒退上坡、空中转向等动作。Gene Munster对那场发布会的评价是"一次工程炫技"，并说马斯克"等不及"要合并。


然而，业务能够深度合作，并不能直接证明股权必须合并。特别委员会需要回答的核心问题是：合作产生的新增价值是否足以抵消交易成本、监管摩擦和整合风险。

"特斯拉为SpaceX输血"的叙事，数字并不支撑

合并传闻中，一个直观的说法是：SpaceX大建AI基础设施，特斯拉可以提供现金流。这一说法抓住了SpaceX资本开支庞大的事实，却高估了特斯拉眼下可供调配的资金。


据彭博一致预期，特斯拉2030年自由现金流约120亿美元，而SpaceX预计届时消耗约170亿美元——两者方向相反。更近的数字同样不乐观：特斯拉第二季度自由现金流为负11亿美元；分析师预测其第三季度自由现金流均值为负45亿美元，2026年全年约为负97亿美元。与此同时，SpaceX截至9月底持有约513亿美元现金及386亿美元有价证券，资金状况并不匮乏。


合并不会凭空增加一美元现金，它可能改变的是融资方式和资本配置权限——哪些项目由合并后的公司统一建设，哪些成本由不同业务共同承担，以及投资者愿意为这一整套计划提供多少资本。


对马斯克而言，统一配置资源或许更高效；对特斯拉股东而言，问题在于汽车、储能和机器人业务创造的价值，将如何分配给SpaceX的算力、卫星和航天项目。若交易方案说不清这一点，"协同"反而会成为资本开支失控的担忧。

控制权结构，可能是交易设计里最关键的一笔

分析师普遍认为，这笔交易在经济利益之外还有另一层逻辑——控制权。


巴克莱测算，马斯克持有SpaceX约48%的经济权益，通过每股10倍投票权的B类股掌握约82%的投票权；在特斯拉持股约20%，折算后接近17%的投票权。若SpaceX按当前估值以换股方式收购特斯拉，他在合并后公司中大约持有37%的经济权益，控制约56%的投票权。RBC的口径稍有差异，认为马斯克掌握SpaceX 85%的投票权，但方向一致：交易会把"经济权益不到四成、投票权过半"这个结构复制到一家3.5万亿美元量级的公司身上。


马斯克曾公开表示，他希望持有特斯拉约25%的股权，才足以维持对AI和机器人战略的影响力，而目前仍有差距。这笔交易可以利用SpaceX的双层股权结构补上这个缺口。


这一点直接影响谈判难度。马斯克本人已承认存在利益冲突，不能参与特别委员会的讨论。委员会不仅要评估业务协同，还要确定各自估值、换股比例、可能的溢价，以及不同类别股东在合并后各自拥有多少经济权益和投票权。

真正握着否决权的，是华盛顿

路透社将地缘政治和监管列为合并的"最大挑战"：SpaceX是美国军方、情报机构和NASA的主要承包商，Starshield已被用于战场通信，马斯克和特朗普均否认对其设限，但这套系统的军事敏感性已毋庸置疑。


因此，对合并的审查维度将从反垄断扩展到国家安全。反垄断审查、双方股东与董事会批准、外国投资审查，三道程序中任何一道卡住，交易的形态都会发生变化。这种类型的交易在商业史上没有先例，也不存在现成的监管模板。

盘面给出答案，但定价有待细化

特别委员会消息确认后，SpaceX盘后最多涨约8.6%，特斯拉仅涨约1.8%，SPCX盘前一度报161.18美元，较收盘价高约9%。

马斯克先说自己是在"雷区里跳踢踏舞"。几秒之后还是给了答案，合并"有很多好处"。Deepwater Asset Management 的 Gene Munster 事后数了数，这句话他讲了大概三遍。
这让一个谈论已久的设想进入了正式评估阶段：彭博指出，特斯拉市值约 1.5 万亿美元，SpaceX 约 2 万亿美元，合在一起 3.5 万亿。
会不会合并，已经不该是问题。巴克莱在 10 月 14 日的报告认为，两家合并的可能性"已经越来越成为共识预期"。股东名册高度重叠，SpaceX 买特斯拉的 Cybertruck，又通过 xAI 买公用事业级储能电池。今年 9 月的 All-In 峰会上，马斯克被问到为什么两家公司要分开，他反问："这么多层面都在合作，谁能想象在如此紧密的合作下会采取什么行动。"

马斯克列举的合作清单涵盖超级智能软件、芯片设计、Terafab、机器人、轨道数据中心和连接服务。这些项目不断碰到同一批资源：芯片、能源、制造能力，以及能够持续支付建设成本的资本。"简化决策"是合并动机中排名靠前的一项——许多跨公司项目需要两个董事会和两批股东分别点头。

合并传闻中，一个直观的说法是：SpaceX大建AI基础设施，特斯拉可以提供现金流。这一说法抓住了SpaceX资本开支庞大的事实，却高估了特斯拉眼下可供调配的资金。

对马斯克而言，统一配置资源或许更高效；对特斯拉股东而言，问题在于汽车、储能和机器人业务创造的价值，将如何分配给SpaceX的算力、卫星和航天项目。若交易方案说不清这一点，"协同"反而会成为资本开支失控的担忧。

巴克莱测算，马斯克持有SpaceX约48%的经济权益，通过每股10倍投票权的B类股掌握约82%的投票权；在特斯拉持股约20%，折算后接近17%的投票权。若SpaceX按当前估值以换股方式收购特斯拉，他在合并后公司中大约持有37%的经济权益，控制约56%的投票权。RBC的口径稍有差异，认为马斯克掌握SpaceX 85%的投票权，但方向一致：交易会把"经济权益不到四成、投票权过半"这个结构复制到一家3.5万亿美元量级的公司身上。
马斯克曾公开表示，他希望持有特斯拉约25%的股权，才足以维持对AI和机器人战略的影响力，而目前仍有差距。这笔交易可以利用SpaceX的双层股权结构补上这个缺口。
这一点直接影响谈判难度。马斯克本人已承认存在利益冲突，不能参与特别委员会的讨论。委员会不仅要评估业务协同，还要确定各自估值、换股比例、可能的溢价，以及不同类别股东在合并后各自拥有多少经济权益和投票权。

因此，对合并的审查维度将从反垄断扩展到国家安全。反垄断审查、双方股东与董事会批准、外国投资审查，三道程序中任何一道卡住，交易的形态都会发生变化。这种类型的交易在商业史上没有先例，也不存在现成的监管模板。

items.text:
Elon Musk has said he is actively considering merging Tesla and SpaceX, his two biggest companies.

"Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said during a call with financial analysts to discuss SpaceX's latest results on Tuesday.

While Musk noted it could not be assumed a merger will go ahead, and it would need shareholders' support, he said special committees within both companies had been formed to examine the move.

"The special committees have not reached agreement on terms of any transaction and there's no guarantee that they will," he said. "But I do think there is a lot of merit to merging and a lot to be gained."

With Tesla valued at roughly $1.5 trillion (£1.1 trillion) and SpaceX at $2 trillion, a combination of the two companies would mark one of the largest mergers in history.

SpaceX builds space rockets as well as Starlink internet satellites and provides a secured satellite network for governments, including the US, through its Starshield business.

That part of the business is currently facing scrutiny over claims Ukraine's access to the network has been limited, leaving it vulnerable to deadly strikes by Russia.

US President Donald Trump has denied either he or Musk ordered the slowdown. Musk himself suggested the US government might have been behind the restrictions.

Starlink's total revenue rose to $5.2bn in the three months to 30 September from $3bn in the same period last year. It is dwarfed by SpaceX's expansion into offering cloud compute capacity for other tech companies, such as Anthropic and Google.

The business generated revenues of $7.5bn over the three months, up from $813m last year.

Musk, who became the world's first paper trillionaire after the SpaceX stock market debut earlier this year, said he is not included in either of the special committees considering the mega-merger.

He described himself as a "conflicted party" as the chief executive of both Tesla and SpaceX.

Even commenting on the possibility of combining the two companies, Musk compared it to "tap dancing through a minefield".

A merger would ultimately be decided by shareholders, he added. At least 50% of Tesla's shareholders would need to approve a combination, which Musk described as "quite a high hurdle to achieve".

Shareholders have supported Musk's desires before. Last year, a majority of investors in Tesla approved a compensation package for Musk valued at around $1tn.

While Tesla is known as an electric car company, Musk has lately been shifting resources there to work around robotics.

SpaceX, with its growing focus on AI infrastructure, quickly outstripped Tesla on the stock market in terms of value when it made its market debut in June.

SpaceX, as a whole is not profitable, despite revenue jumping to $27bn from $13.7bn over the first nine months of the year.

Over that same period it lost $1.1bn although it did report a $4.4bn profit for the most recent three months.

Following Musk's comments, SpaceX's share price rose 8% in after-hours trading. Shares in Tesla, which reports its own quarterly results on Wednesday, rose by 2%

Over the last year, Musk has taken to bringing more of his companies under fewer banners. Before it went public earlier this year, SpaceX acquired xAI and X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, both of which Musk owned.

The recent launch of Terafab, a combined effort to manufacture computer chips between Tesla and SpaceX, was another signal that Musk sees his companies as potentially more effective when working together.

Musk said on Tuesday a full merger between the two companies would make sense for the work each is doing around chips, artificial intelligence and software.

items.title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?
items.summary:
Elon Musk has spent years building Tesla and SpaceX into a pair of trillion-dollar technology empires. Now, he is considering bringing them together.

Asked on
items.text:
Elon Musk has spent years building Tesla and SpaceX into a pair of trillion-dollar technology empires. Now, he is considering bringing them together.

Asked on Tuesday whether a merger would be a good idea, Musk was clear: "Yes."

The prospect is more than hypothetical. Musk said special committees have been formed to assess a potential deal, although he stressed that there is no guarantee a merger will happen and that nothing has been agreed.

With Tesla valued at roughly $1.5 trillion (£1.1 trillion) and SpaceX at $2 trillion, a combination of the two companies would mark the largest merger ever.

Any deal would also need shareholder backing. But Musk said he saw "a lot to be gained" in bringing the businesses together.

"In my opinion, 100%. It's just a question of when," says David Nicholson, chief technology advisor at market research firm The Futurum Group.

The unveiling of the Tesla Roadster last week - a futuristic electric car powered by SpaceX rocket thrusters - served as a "symbolic embodiment" hinting at the two Musk companies merging, Nicholson said.

Musk, chief executive of both SpaceX and Tesla, said bringing the firms together would be beneficial given the work each does around chips, artificial intelligence (AI) and other technology projects.

Specifically, the deal would combine Tesla's cars, robots and self-driving technology with SpaceX's rockets, data centres, satellites and telecommunications operations.

The move could be a step towards Musk's mission to build a self-sustaining city on Mars - a vision that has invited sceptics but also plenty of backers.

Over the past year, Musk has moved to consolidate his businesses, with SpaceX acquiring xAI and X, formerly Twitter, before going public this year.

But the merger would ultimately be decided by shareholders, with half of Tesla's needed to back the deal, a threshold even Musk described as "quite a high hurdle".

Musk, as boss of both companies, cannot participate in shareholder discussions.

Even so, Musk, a key shareholder of Tesla, will likely get his way in the next few years, said investment analyst Dan Sheehan from Telos Wealth Advisors.

He believes shareholders will back the deal as the technology the companies develop complement each other, Sheehan said.

But the merger would mean that Tesla shareholders will likely hold a "smaller slice of a much larger and more complex business," he added.

"There's no real precedent for how a public company like Tesla gets priced in this," Sheehan said.

SpaceX shares rose 8% in after hours trading while shares of Tesla climbed by 2%.

Experts told the BBC that Tesla drivers are unlikely to see much drastic change in the near term, even if the two companies combine.

In fact, vehicles seem almost like "an afterthought", overshadowed by the potential to combine the Tesla and SpaceX's tech capabilities, Nicholson said.

Changes are already underway at Tesla. The carmaker said earlier this year that it would prioritise its best-selling Model Y and Model 3, shifting focus away from less popular models.

Tesla also started using a manufacturing plant in California to produce humanoid robots, known as Optimus.

Pairing Tesla's self-driving technology and robotics with SpaceX's AI and satellite network could result in more capable vehicles, Sheehan said.

"The question is how much priority cars get inside a company increasingly driven by AI infrastructure," he added.

The recent Roadster showcase suggests SpaceX technology could be pulled into future Tesla products, which could attract more customers, said Tu Le, the founder of advisory firm Sino Auto Insights.

The Cybertruck-maker faces intense competition from Chinese carmakers like BYD, which overtook Tesla as the world's biggest EV maker in January.

The biggest winner is probably Musk - the world's richest man who also became the world's first trillionaire earlier this year.

The merger would give Musk greater voting control over the combined company than he currently has at Tesla, a factor the special committee assessing the deal would have to consider.

A single company makes it easier for Musk to run his AI strategy the way he wants, Sheehan said.

"The deal itself doesn't add to Musk's wealth, but it concentrates it further in one stock," he said.

However, the merger could attract scrutiny over Musk, already a polarising figure in the US, Nicholson said.

The move could also face more regulatory pressure if Democrats - many of whom have been critical of Musk - win more seats in the US midterm elections next month.

Shareholders have backed Musk's desires before. Last year, Tesla investors approved an unprecedented compensation package for Musk valued around $1tn.

"I honestly don't think Musk will be keeping track of what the merger will do for his wealth," Nicholson said.

The deal also brings Musk closer to what Nicholson says is "his mission in life": colonising Mars.

items.text:
Speech transcription and voice generation have come a long way, but building end-to-end voice agents that can listen, reason, interact, and handle complex workflows remains difficult.

A reliable voice agent needs to do four things very well (and simultaneously):

Listen accurately across languages, accents, speakers, and interruptions,

Reason deeply about what users mean in specific contexts,

Speak naturally with emotion and expression, and

Take action over multiple steps through connected systems.

Getting all four to work together reliably in real time remains a challenge.

To address this, we introduce Voxtral 3: a new family of state-of-the-art speech-to-text and text-to-speech models, alongside a voice agent SDK that brings listening, thinking, tool calling, and speaking into a single real-time streaming pipeline.

Voxtral 3 is built to create natural conversational experiences, from contact-center agents and service desks to virtual assistants and hands-free copilots. With support for dozens of languages, expressive speech, complex reasoning, and deep integration with your own tools and data, agents built with Voxtral can interpret nuanced intent, reason through sophisticated requests, and execute multi-step actions across connected systems.

As with other Mistral models, the Voxtral 3 family is designed for sovereign deployment. Available today through Mistral's EU-hosted API or for self-deployment on your own infrastructure, it gives organizations control over where audio is processed, how data is handled, and whether conversations are retained.

Highlights

Accurate transcription across 50+ languages. The speech-to-text model, Voxtral Small Transcribe 3, is state-of-the-art in multilingual transcription, identifying who said what (diarization), using keyphrases to improve its accuracy (context-biasing). It detects when someone has finished speaking so agents can respond without delay (end-of-turn detection).

Natural speech that adapts to the conversation. The text-to-speech model, Voxtral Mini TTS 3, introduces new voices that adjust their emotion, pace, and emphasis based on conversational context, with support for 35+ languages and 50+ dialects.

Human-like intelligence at your (spoken) command. The new voice agent SDK combines listening, reasoning, tool calling, and speaking into a real-time experience. Agents can retrieve information, interact with business systems, and complete tasks during live conversations over phone or web.

Pro Voice for distinctly accurate voice adaptation. For professional use cases where basic voice cloning does not suffice, Voxtral’s Pro Voice adaptation is able to reproduce a speaker’s distinctive character, emotional range, and speaking style across languages, using just 30 minutes of audio.

Your voice AI, on your infrastructure. Use Mistral's EU-hosted API or deploy Voxtral 3 on your own infrastructure. Keep sensitive conversations within your environment and control whether any audio is retained.

Try Voxtral now | Learn more

It hears 50+ languages, with state-of-the-art accuracy.

Voxtral Transcribe 3 represents a significant milestone across transcription, diarization (who spoke when) and context biasing capabilities. The supported list of languages is expanded to 50, including 24 official EU languages and many low-resource Asian and Indic languages.

The Small version achieves state-of-the-art results across diarization and multilingual transcription, including in English, French and Spanish. It outperforms Whisper, Scribe v2 and Gemini 3.5 Transcribe. The Mini variant is 4B parameters, enabling fast and accurate transcriptions at a price of $0.0035/min.

Both models support context biasing, where key terms and free-form text can be given to bias the transcription and improve recall on technical terms. This enables them to be used in production settings with domain-specific vocabulary without the need for fine-tuning.

Voxtral Transcribe 3 represents a significant milestone across transcription, diarization (who spoke when) and context biasing capabilities. The supported list of languages is expanded to 50, including 24 official EU languages and many low-resource Asian and Indic languages.

The Small version achieves state-of-the-art results across diarization and multilingual transcription, including in English, French and Spanish. It outperforms Whisper, Scribe v2 and Gemini 3.5 Transcribe. The Mini variant is 4B parameters, enabling fast and accurate transcriptions at a price of $0.0035/min.

Both models support context biasing, where key terms and free-form text can be given to bias the transcription and improve recall on technical terms. This enables them to be used in production settings with domain-specific vocabulary without the need for fine-tuning.

At $13 per 1M characters, Voxtral Speech 3 costs less to run than comparable models from OpenAI TTS-1, Deepgram, ElevenLabs Flash and Gemini Flash.

The speech model implicitly interprets the semantic meaning of context better, producing natural speech across a diverse range of emotions and languages. New and improved features include voice cloning from 30+ minutes of sampled audio, custom prompt instruction following (IF), contextual TTS, and a vocabulary library, all of which serve the goal of speech reliability in deployment. The voice agent is in control of the whole conversation.

Voxtral 3 introduces a voice agent SDK, built on LiveKit, that runs speech in, reasoning, and speech out as one streaming pipeline. Voxtral Mini Transcribe Realtime 3 listens and detects when the caller has finished speaking, a general model—like Mistral Small—reasons and calls tools, and Voxtral Speech 3 replies in the tone of the conversation so far. No stage waits for the one before it, so each turn completes in under one second, and the agent stops talking when the caller cuts in.

During a call, the agent can verify a caller's identity, check a bill, or book an appointment, using function calling, web search, and retrieval over your own systems. It answers and places calls over SIP, runs in browsers and apps over WebRTC, and connects to the telephony, IVR, and contact-center software you already use.
